texts.preamble: Rajendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 January, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ? Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:11094 Court No. - 74 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 1051 of 2018 Revisionist :- Rajendra Singh Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :- Lokendra Pratap Singh,Ashutosh Pratap Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: 5. The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 21.12.2002 at about 12 p.m. Food Inspector Dev Raj Singh saw the revisionist displaying buffalo milk for sale near a school in Borikalan. He then during his checking purchased 750 ml of milk and sealed it as per the rules for being sent to the food analyst for inspection. The material was inspected by the food analyst and his report dated 02.02.2003 stated that milk fat is deficient by 7% and milk solids not fat is also deficient by 7%. A complaint was filed after which notice u/s 13 (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was sent to the revisionist who exercised his option of getting the milk tested through Central Food Laboratory after which the material was sent to the Central Food Laboratory, Mysore who vide its report dated 17.06.2011 opined that the sample does not conform to the standards laid down for Buffalo Milk under the provision of PFA Act 1954 & Rules since milk fat was found to be 5.5% whereas as per the standards it could not have been less than 6%. The opinion as drawn is as follows:- "Milk fat content falls below the minimum standard limit." 6. The trial started in which the statement of the complainant Dev Raj Sigh was recorded u/s 244 Cr.P.C. as P.W.-1. There was no other witness produced u/s 244 Cr.P.C. Subsequently u/s 246 Cr.P.C. the complainant Dev Raj Sigh, Food Inspector was produced and examined as P.W.-1. Anil Kumar Bhardwaj the Food Clerk was examined as P.W.-2. After completion of evidence of the said witnesses, the accused in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated in his additional submissions that he does not do the work of milk. In his defence he produced Bhoori Singh the Village Pradhan as D.W.-1 and Narendra Pal Singh as D.W.-2.
texts.arguments: 7. Learned counsel for the revisionist raised two arguments in the matter which are as under:- (i) There is a difference in the report of the two analysts in as much as the report of the public analyst states of milk fat deficient by 7% and also milk solids not fat deficient by 7% but the Central Food Laboratory after its test quantified the milk fat to be present in the sample as 5.5% whereas as per the standards it could not have been less than 6% and had thus opined that milk fat contents was below the standard Rajendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192076732/ 2 limit. It is submitted that there is a difference in the report of both the analysts with regards to contents of the milk fat and as such it would be unsafe to rely upon them to come to a conclusion that milk was adulterated. (ii) The case of the revisionist-accused is that he does not do work of milk which is stated by him in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. The two defence witnesses produced by him also state of the same that he does not do work of milk and is a farmer having agricultural land. The trial court has without cogent reasons disbelieved the said witnesses and the conclusion as dawn by the trial court is that since the witnesses are of the same village they are stating in favour of the revisionist-accused. It is submitted that the said approach is not a legal approach and the testimony of the said defence witnesses stands unblemished which should have been given credence and accepted by the trial court. 8. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that looking to the said two arguments the present revision deserves to be allowed and conviction & sentence of the revisionist be set-aside. 9. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the trial court has returned cogent and well-found findings while convicting the revisionist. It is submitted that the appellate court has also exercised its discretion on the basis of material available on record without any error apparent on the face of it.
